name: Troubadour Culture and Courtly Love
summary: The troubadour movement, originating in Occitan-speaking southern France with Duke William IX of Aquitaine, creates Europe's first major vernacular literary culture. Troubadours compose lyric poetry in Occitan celebrating fin'amors (courtly love), a complex code of idealized love and service to a lady. The tradition spreads to northern France (trouvères), Germany (Minnesingers), and Iberia (troubadours), creating the literary foundations of European romance traditions.

_quarry.structural_significance: The troubadour movement is the origin of European secular lyric poetry; the promotion of vernacular Occitan as a literary language (rather than Latin) prefigures the later development of French, Italian, and Spanish as literary languages; the ideals of courtly love reshape aristocratic behavior codes and social expectations; the Albigensian Crusade's destruction of Occitan culture (1209-1229) permanently damages this literary tradition
